title: What does FinCEN and the BSA mean for agent payments?
abstract: Sourced explanation of FinCEN and the BSA and its practical limits.
body:
According to FinCEN, FinCEN distinguishes users of convertible virtual currency from administrators or exchangers whose activity can constitute money transmission under the Bank Secrecy Act. [1]

Its 2013 guidance says using virtual currency to purchase goods or services on one's own behalf does not alone make that user a money services business. Administrators and exchangers can be money transmitters unless an exemption or limitation applies. The 2019 guidance applies that framework to additional business models; it does not create a universal exemption for software that uses a blockchain. [1][2]

For an agent payment service, assess the parties, control over funds and actual service before drawing a legal conclusion about FinCEN and the BSA. Testnet execution demonstrates a mechanism with faucet assets; it does not establish licensing, safeguarding or real-customer compliance. A small payment or an automated decision is not evidence of an exemption. The cited authority describes a framework, not a legal opinion about this product. [1]

Author interpretation: map the proposed business flow to the current rules with qualified local advice, preserve the basis for each conclusion and revisit it when the flow changes. Keep personal information out of public ledger memos and use appropriate private channels for necessary information exchange. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
